scheme_name: Adi Dravidar and Tribal Welfare Department: Scholarship-Public Examination Fee for 10th and 12th Std.
description:
The Adi Dravidar and Tribal Welfare Department in India has implemented a scholarship scheme aimed at supporting students from marginalized communities.

This scheme specifically targets students belonging to Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.

The scholarship was initiated to alleviate the financial burden of public examination fees for students in the 10th and 12th grades.

The scheme was launched in the year 2008.

Its primary objective is to ensure that students from economically disadvantaged backgrounds can complete their secondary and higher secondary education without the hindrance of examination fees.

The scheme aims to increase the enrollment and retention rates of students from these communities in schools.

The targeted enrollment increase is set at 10 percent annually.

The scholarship covers the entire examination fee for both the 10th and 12th standard public examinations.

For the 10th standard, the examination fee is approximately INR 500.

For the 12th standard, the examination fee can go up to INR 800.

This financial assistance is crucial as it directly impacts the ability of students to appear for their board examinations.

The scholarship also aims to promote educational equity among marginalized communities.

Eligibility for this scholarship is strictly defined.

Students must belong to Scheduled Caste or Scheduled Tribe categories as recognized by the Government of India.

They must be enrolled in government or government-aided schools.

Students must be in the 10th or 12th standard to qualify for the scholarship.

There is no upper age limit specified for applicants.

However, students must have a family income that does not exceed INR 2 lakh per annum.

This income criterion ensures that the benefits reach the most economically disadvantaged families.

The application process for the scholarship is straightforward.

Students must obtain the application form from their respective schools.

The form can also be downloaded from the official website of the Adi Dravidar and Tribal Welfare Department.

Once the form is filled out, it must be submitted to the school authorities.

The school will then verify the details and forward the application to the district welfare office.

Required documents include a caste certificate issued by a competent authority.

Students must also provide proof of income such as an income certificate from the local revenue office.

Additionally, a copy of the student’s Aadhaar card is required for identification.

The application must be submitted before the deadline set by the department.

Typically, the application period opens in January and closes in February each year.

Disbursement of the scholarship amount occurs shortly after the application process is completed.

The funds are directly transferred to the respective school accounts.

This ensures that the examination fees are paid on behalf of the students.

The department aims to complete the disbursement process within one month of the application deadline.

The Adi Dravidar and Tribal Welfare Department is responsible for the implementation of this scheme.

The department operates under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment.

It has various district offices across states to facilitate the application process.

Contact details for the department can be found on the official government website.

Students can reach out to their local district welfare office for assistance.

The scheme has seen a significant uptake since its inception.

In the year 2021 alone, over 1 lakh students benefited from the scholarship.

This number has been steadily increasing each year.

The government allocates a budget specifically for this scholarship scheme.

In the 2022-2023 fiscal year, the budget allocation was approximately INR 50 crore.

This financial commitment underscores the government’s dedication to promoting education among marginalized communities.

The scholarship not only covers examination fees but also aims to reduce dropout rates.

Data indicates that dropout rates among Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe students have decreased by 15 percent since the launch of this scheme.

The program also includes awareness campaigns to inform eligible students about the scholarship.

These campaigns are conducted in schools and community centers.

The department collaborates with NGOs to reach out to students in remote areas.

Feedback from beneficiaries indicates a high level of satisfaction with the scheme.

Many students have reported that the scholarship has relieved their families of financial stress.

This has allowed them to focus more on their studies.

The scholarship scheme is part of a broader initiative by the Indian government to enhance educational opportunities for marginalized communities.

It aligns with the Sustainable Development Goals set by the United Nations.

The government aims to ensure inclusive and equitable quality education.

The scholarship also encourages students to pursue higher education after completing their 12th standard.

Many beneficiaries have gone on to enroll in colleges and universities.

This has a positive ripple effect on the community as educated individuals contribute to societal development.

The scheme is regularly reviewed and updated based on feedback and changing needs.

The department is committed to making the application process as user-friendly as possible.

In recent years, efforts have been made to digitize the application process.

This includes online submission of applications and tracking of scholarship status.

The initiative has made it easier for students to apply from remote locations.

Overall, the Adi Dravidar and Tribal Welfare Department’s scholarship for public examination fees is a vital initiative.

It plays a crucial role in promoting educational equity.

The scheme has a significant impact on the lives of students from marginalized communities.

By alleviating financial burdens, it empowers students to pursue their educational aspirations.
